description:
Write the no-follow open of a leaf file once in the storage capability module and build every reader that opens a repository file on it: the storage readers, the profile package reader (deleting profile's own opener module) and `read_exact_store`.

## Background

- The sequence lstat leaf, refuse a symlink or non-file, open with `FollowSymlinks::No`, then `fstat` the handle again is written out in `open_regular_file_nofollow` (`crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store.rs:1645-1661`), `read_repository_file_nofollow` (`:1695-1730`) and `read_confined_relative` (`:1749-1813`), and partly in `inspect_capability_leaf` (`:1456-1511`; lstat at `:1461`, open at `:1481` with no handle recheck). `open_child_dir_nofollow` (`:1619-1641`) repeats the lstat-then-open pattern for directories (lstat `:1624`, handle check `:1635`). All five functions live in `crates/jit/src/storage/capability_fs.rs` and return its own error type; the line numbers name their former home in the session module, where today's code can be read.
- The leading lstat exists so a FIFO or device is refused before a blocking open. A non-blocking open (`_cap_fs_ext_nonblock(true)`), as the profile package reader already uses, returns at once on such an entry, so the handle's own metadata can refuse it and the separate lstat is redundant.
- `crates/jit/src/profile/nofollow.rs` builds a second set of no-follow read options (`read_options`, `:31-38`: read, no-follow, maybe-dir, non-blocking) and exposes `open_entry_nofollow` (`:42-47`), `open_path_nofollow` (`:51-57`), `OpenRefusal` with `classify_open_failure` (`:60-99`) and `is_executable` (`:102-113`). Its callers are `crates/jit/src/profile/package.rs:2` (directory walk through `DirEntry`, opens at `:480`, `:504`) and `crates/jit/src/profile/package_capture.rs:31` (declared repository files through an anchored `Dir`, open at `:405`; module rustdoc `:21`). `crates/jit/src/profile/mod.rs:12` declares the module.
- Profile production code imports nothing from `storage` today; profile is not a pure layer (it already does file I/O through `cap_std`), so importing the storage primitive keeps dependencies pointing at storage, which owns persistence (`@/inv/architecture-dependency-direction`).
- `test_profile_package_reads_build_no_follow_options_in_one_place` (`crates/jit/tests/scratch_build/repository_state_cutover_tests.rs:1467`) pins the profile opener to `nofollow.rs` by finding the modules under `src/profile` that call `_cap_fs_ext_follow`.
- `read_exact_store` (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:77-172`) reads one data root without aggregation; callers are `commands/worktree.rs:347-348` and the test at `json.rs:2116` (calls `:2188`, `:2199`). For each issue record (`:116-137`) and for the event log (`:142-169`) it runs its own sequence: `symlink_metadata`, refuse a symlink or non-file, `open_regular_file_nofollow`, `read_to_end`/`read_to_string`.
- Storage has one no-follow leaf read over a held parent directory (non-blocking open, `fstat` recheck that the leaf is a regular file, `None` for an absent leaf), built on by `read_repository_file_nofollow`. Gate-run records are already read through one shared reader in both backends.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One function in the storage capability module opens a leaf no-follow and non-blocking and returns a handle only for a regular file (one for a directory where a directory is wanted); `open_regular_file_nofollow`, `read_repository_file_nofollow`, `read_confined_relative`, `inspect_capability_leaf`'s file branch and `open_child_dir_nofollow` call it and build no open options of their own.
- [hard] REQ-02: The primitive's own tests show a symlink leaf, a directory, a FIFO and an absent leaf each produce the same outcome the readers report today (unsafe target, unsafe target, unsafe target without blocking, absence), on the filesystem backend.
- [hard] REQ-03: `crates/jit/src/profile/nofollow.rs` is deleted; `package.rs` and `package_capture.rs` open entries through the storage capability module, which provides the entry and anchored-path opens, the open-failure classification and the executable-mode test they use. No module under `crates/jit/src/profile` builds no-follow open options, and the cutover guard asserts that profile names no `_cap_fs_ext_follow` call while the storage capability module holds the read options.
- [hard] REQ-04: `read_exact_store` reads each issue record and the event log through the shared no-follow leaf read; it calls no `symlink_metadata` on a leaf and no `open_regular_file_nofollow` of its own. The gate-run readers in `json.rs` keep their sequence for 0851fae4, which rewrites them behind one reader.
- [hard] REQ-05: A symlinked issue record, a symlinked event log and a FIFO record each fail `read_exact_store` without hanging, and an absent issue directory or event log contributes no records, shown by `read_exact_store` tests.
- [hard] REQ-06: The profile package suites (symlink, FIFO, escape and executable-mode cases) pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged: each reader keeps its absent, unsafe and I/O outcomes, the profile opens keep their options, refusals and classifications, and the one change is that a FIFO issue record in `read_exact_store` is refused without blocking.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: The no-follow leaf open exists once and serves storage, profile and exact-store reads
